goal: Go from zero ML knowledge to training and evaluating a small image classifier in PyTorch
interpretation: The learner can explain how neural networks learn (loss, gradient descent, backprop), and can write, train and evaluate a small CNN image classifier in PyTorch from scratch, understanding overfitting and metrics.
assumptions: The 1200 minutes is pure viewing time, so long code-along courses are acceptable and no time is reserved for separate practice.
A small image classifier means something like MNIST/Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10 trained with a CNN.
Because the learner knows calculus and linear algebra, math explanations can be intuitive but not simplified to avoid derivatives or matrices.
No constraints rule out particular video titles, so title exclusions are empty.

sub_topics.title: Machine learning fundamentals: supervised learning, loss functions, train/test split
sub_topics.why: Learner has zero ML background; needs the vocabulary and framing before touching neural networks, though numpy and linear algebra let them move quickly.

sub_topics.title: Gradient descent, neural networks and backpropagation with math intuition
sub_topics.why: Learner knows calculus, so the chain rule view of backprop will click fast; this gives the intuition they want for why training works.

sub_topics.title: PyTorch tensors and autograd
sub_topics.why: Learner knows numpy, so PyTorch tensors map onto familiar ideas; autograd connects directly to the backprop they just learned.

sub_topics.title: Building models and training loops in PyTorch (nn.Module, optimizers, DataLoader)
sub_topics.why: Needed to turn the math into working code, including batching, loss, optimizer steps and GPU/CPU handling.

sub_topics.title: Convolutional neural networks for images
sub_topics.why: Image classification needs convolutions, pooling and feature maps; the learner's linear algebra background helps with understanding the operations.

sub_topics.title: Model evaluation, overfitting, and regularization
sub_topics.why: The learner must measure accuracy on held-out data, read loss curves, and use techniques like augmentation, dropout and weight decay to reduce overfitting.

sub_topics.title: Build, train and evaluate an image classifier end-to-end in PyTorch
sub_topics.why: A code-along project ties everything together on a dataset like CIFAR-10 or Fashion-MNIST and matches the stated goal.
